messages.subject: model definitions
parts:
I am using Distance4.1 w/ a relatively simple (but large)10-min
point count dataset. Our study areas are arranged into transects and
pts. w/ each point in a specific habitat and each bird observation
recorded w/ an approximate distance. I want to make some comparisons
across areas/habitats/species using distance estimates and have figured
out the software for the most part. I have received some advise/done
some research and decided an estimate per point is appropriate even
though some are using a small sample size to get the estimate...........

My question is regarding the model definition. I was hoping to get some
advice on what is appropriate for this type of analysis? I've played
around w/ the various options and get quite a bit of variance in the
density estimates? Should I just go w/ the default? I've found papers
where the researchers have used Distance for their analyses, but haven't
found specifics on what inputs were used?

I'd appreciate any advice.

Bonnie Hunt
